chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about a man afflicted by dripping from his private part, whether blood or something else. He said: “Let him make a pouch, perform wudu (ablution), and pray, for that is only an affliction with which he has been tried. He should not repeat [the prayer] except due to the hadath from which wudu (ablution) is performed.”

key_terms.الْحَدَثِ: the state that nullifies ritual purity and requires wudu (ablution)
key_terms.خَرِيطَةً: a pouch or cloth-device used to contain the discharge

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who has continuous discharge and wants to perform salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one afflicted with continual discharge from the private part, whether blood or otherwise. He is instructed to take practical measures, perform wudu (ablution), and continue his salat (prayer), since this is a condition of affliction and does not by itself require repeating the prayer except in the case of a nullifying hadath.
